title: improv·artist · chromatic (Gerhard Richter)
mutation_directive: improv artist: chromatic via Gerhard Richter

improv_extras.practice: color-grid charts, squeegee abstracts; randomness as method

v1.feedback: The Richter color-chart concept is legibly translated — grid structure, cell-level hue assignment, and edge-bias clustering are all present and idea-driven. However, additive blending across a full-spectrum HSL palette will wash overlapping cells toward white, undermining the crisp tile boundaries that make Richter's charts readable; switch to normal blending or premultiplied alpha. The morph between two random fields is conceptually correct but visually low-contrast since spatial layout barely changes — consider a squeegee-drag animation (horizontal smear per row with staggered timing) to make the randomness-as-method feel embodied rather than just a lerp between two static states.

v2.feedback: The Richter color-chart-as-tower-silhouette is legible and the squeegee sweep genuinely drives the motion rather than being decorative — good marriage of the 5gm vertical direction with the linked idea. The full-hue palette risks reading as chaotic at a glance; consider biasing toward 3-4 dominant hue clusters per sweep cycle (as Richter's physical charts often have regional hue gravity) while keeping the full range available. The smear displacement is subtle enough that on first load the piece reads as static — increase smearWidth or add a faint directional streak trail so the squeegee process is visible within the first 2 seconds without waiting for a full cycle.
